claim: Hundreds of millions of people will starve to death in the 1970s.
madeBy: Paul R. Ehrlich, The Population Bomb
criteria: Famine deaths on the order of hundreds of millions during 1970–1979.
evidence: Famine deaths in the 1970s were tragic but far below that scale, while world food output rose with the Green Revolution.

claim: Inflation-adjusted prices of copper, chromium, nickel, tin and tungsten will rise between 1980 and 1990 (Ehrlich's side of the Simon–Ehrlich wager).
madeBy: Paul Ehrlich and colleagues, wager with Julian Simon
criteria: The combined inflation-adjusted price of the five metals is higher in 1990 than in 1980.
evidence: All five metals fell in inflation-adjusted price; Ehrlich paid Simon.

claim: Western America breaks up, most of Japan goes into the sea, northern Europe changes suddenly, between 1958 and 1998.
criteria: Any of the named large-scale geological changes occurs by the end of 1998.
evidence: None of the named changes occurred within the window.

claim: The world will come to an end in 1881.
evidence: It did not; the verses were also confessed as a forgery in 1873.

claim: The world ends or is transformed catastrophically on 21 December 2012 (modern popular reading).
madeBy: Popular 2012 phenomenon authors (not the Maya inscription)
criteria: A global catastrophe on or about 21 December 2012.
evidence: The date passed without catastrophe. The Classic Maya inscription itself never predicted one.

claim: Christ will return on 22 October 1844 (calculated from Daniel 8:14).
madeBy: Millerite movement (Samuel S. Snow, William Miller)
criteria: The Second Advent occurs on 22 October 1844.
evidence: Known as the 'Great Disappointment'. Related text: Book of Daniel (chapter 8 rather than 7).

claim: The Rapture will occur on 21 May 2011.
criteria: A rapture of believers occurs on 21 May 2011.
evidence: Nothing occurred; Camping revised the date to 21 October 2011, which also passed.

claim: It is more probable than not that an ultraintelligent machine will be built within the twentieth century.
criteria: A machine surpassing all human intellectual activity exists by the end of 2000.
evidence: No such machine existed by 2000. Good's broader thesis remains open.

claim: A machine will pass a rigorous Turing test by 2029 (Long Bet #1, Kurzweil vs. Kapor).
criteria: Passes the specific multi-judge, two-hour Turing test protocol defined in the Long Bets agreement.
evidence: Resolution date not reached. Claims that current chatbots pass looser Turing-style tests do not resolve this bet.

claim: The Singularity: humans merge with non-biological intelligence, multiplying intelligence about a billion-fold, by 2045.
criteria: Widespread human–machine cognitive merger with a vast increase in effective intelligence.

claim: People will carry pocket wireless instruments that connect the whole earth like a brain, with sight and sound across any distance.
criteria: Mass use of pocket wireless devices for instant global audio and video communication.
evidence: Smartphones on global networks meet the stated description. Caution: the claim was undated, and Tesla's unrealized forecasts are less often counted.

claim: Under business as usual, industrial output and food per person peak and decline sharply in the 21st century.
madeBy: Meadows et al., The Limits to Growth
criteria: Sustained global decline in industrial output and food per capita, in line with the standard-run curves.
evidence: A conditional scenario, not a point forecast. Herrington (2021) found data so far closest to business-as-usual and comprehensive-technology scenarios.

claim: 'This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled.' (Matthew 24:34)
criteria: Depends on reading: Temple destruction (fulfilled 70 CE) or the full return and cosmic signs (not observed).
evidence: Preterists count it fulfilled in 70 CE; others count it unfulfilled or redefine 'generation'. The criteria are contested.

claim: After 'Gloria olivae' comes 'Petrus Romanus', the last pope, followed by the destruction of Rome.
criteria: A pope identifiable as Peter the Roman reigns during persecution, followed by Rome's destruction.
evidence: Francis (2013) and Leo XIV (2025) were not named Peter. Defenders say unnamed popes may intervene, so the claim cannot clearly fail.

claim: The Euphrates will uncover a mountain of gold over which people will fight.
criteria: Gold exposed by the Euphrates, followed by lethal conflict over it.
evidence: River levels fell sharply in 2021–2023 from drought and dams, but no gold was reported. Undated claims cannot fail.

claim: A 'gourd of ashes' will fall from the sky and burn the land.
madeBy: Hopi prophecy as presented by Thomas Banyacya
criteria: A documented pre-1945 statement of the prophecy, matched to the atomic bombings.
evidence: The bombings match the image, but no pre-1945 record of this wording has been documented, so the match may be after the fact.

claim: 'Hister' in Century II.24 foretold Adolf Hitler.
criteria: The 1555 text unambiguously refers to a future German leader.
evidence: 'Hister' was a Latin name for the lower Danube, and the quatrain gives no date. A suggestive resemblance found after the fact.
